item.title: Shibuya Scramble Crossing, Tokyo
item.description: The entire clip is a point-of-view shot from a motorcycle stopped at the iconic Shibuya Scramble Crossing in Tokyo, Japan, featuring numerous distinctive buildings and billboards.
item.evidence: The shot is a wide view of the intersection, with the QFRONT building (housing Tsutaya and Starbucks) and the Shibuya 109 building clearly visible.

holders.notes: The one-minute hero shot visibly includes multiple signs, billboards, LED content, and business marks. Each underlying owner and any advertising-content rights must be assessed separately.

finding.public_domain_rationale: A public crossing is not itself a published copyrighted work. For visible buildings, U.S. Copyright Office guidance states that architectural works created on or after December 1, 1990 may be protected, but 17 U.S.C. §120 permits pictorial representations of a constructed building located in or ordinarily visible from a public place. QFRONT was completed in October 1999 and SHIBUYA109 opened in April 1979, so neither date alone makes the architecture public domain. The U.S. architectural-works exception supports filming or depicting the exteriors from the public crossing, but it does not resolve trademark, advertising, privacy, traffic-permit, or private-property issues; therefore the overall clearance status is unclear rather than safely public domain.
finding.territory_notes: The crossing is a public roadway, but filming may require a Tokyo road-use permit when production activity materially affects ordinary traffic. QFRONT and SHIBUYA109 are privately controlled commercial properties and visible trademarks, signs, LED displays, and other branded elements may require separate permission or clearance for worldwide, all-media, perpetual use. U.S. law generally permits pictorial representations of buildings visible from public places, but that does not grant rights to use trademarks, advertising content, private premises, or identifiable individuals.
finding.licensing_precedent: No documented prior license or reported fee specifically for filming this production view at the actual Shibuya Scramble Crossing was located. Tokyo Location Box documents an official film-commission support channel, and SHIBUYA109 publishes a premises-filming application procedure, but neither establishes a prior license for this exact shot or a standard fee.
unresolved: Current registered title holder and trust structure for each QFRONT condominium interest were not fully identified; TOKYU REIT publicly confirms land ownership and building compartmentalized ownership, while its 2003 filing identifies a Mitsubishi Trust Bank trustee and a predecessor asset-funding seller.

The legal owner of the SHIBUYA109/道玄坂共同ビル real estate was not established from the available records; SHIBUYA109 Entertainment is confirmed as operator and brand company, not conclusively as the building owner.
No direct permission policy or location-license tariff for filming from the public roadway at Shibuya Scramble Crossing was located.
The precise owners and licensing contacts for every visible billboard, LED screen, shop sign, logo, and advertising creative in the one-minute hero shot remain unidentified.

Whether the motorcycle filming itself obstructed traffic, used equipment on the roadway, or was conducted from private property is not documented; those facts determine the applicable permit and property-clearance requirements.
No comprehensive trademark search was completed for every visible mark; QFRONT and SHIBUYA109 rights were only partially documented.

basis.reasoning: The U.S. statute permits pictorial representations of constructed buildings visible from public places, while the Copyright Office explains that architecture created on or after December 1, 1990 can be protected. Because the shot includes buildings and branded material but the public-place architectural exception does not resolve trademark or private-property rights, the overall status is unclear.

citations.title: What Does Copyright Protect? (FAQ) | U.S. Copyright Office
excerpts: What Does Copyright Protect? **What does copyright protect?** Copyright, a form of intellectual property law, protects original works of authorship including literary, dramatic, musical, and artistic works, such as poetry, novels, movies, songs, computer software, and architecture. ... **Can I copyright my website?** The original authorship appearing on a website may be protected by copyright. This includes writings, artwork, photographs, and other forms of authorship protected by copyright. ... No one can lawfully use your photo of your sighting, although someone else may file his own photo of his sighting. Copyright law protects the original photograph, not the subject of the photograph. **Does copyright protect architecture?** Yes. Architectural works became subject to copyright protection on December 1, 1990. The copyright law defines “architectural work” as “the design of a building embodied in any tangible medium of expression, including a building, architectural plans, or drawings.” Copyright protection extends to any architectural work created on or after December 1, 1990. Also, any architectural works that were unconstructed and embodied in unpublished plans or drawings on that date and were constructed by December 31, 2002, are eligible for protection. Architectural designs embodied in buildings constructed prior to December 1, 1990, are not eligible for copyright protection. See [

excerpts: 取材のお申込みについて 取材ご希望の方は、下記いずれかページ内の申し込みフォームより必要事項をご記入の上送信してください。 [](https://shibuya109.jp/coverage-personal) 取材受付のご案内 敷地内で撮影を希望される方は以下の順序に従って申請をお願いいたします。 内容によってはお断りをさせていただく場合もございますので予めご了承ください。 敷地内で撮影を希望される方へ 下記をご一読の上、ページ下記にある「敷地内撮影申込書フォーム」から申請 撮影の日時・場所・内容などが決まり次第、お早目にお送りください。 受付の締め切りは撮影希望日の3日前17時まで（土日祝は日数に含まず）となります。 例)撮影日が火曜日の場合、締め切りは前週の木曜日となります。 TV 番組や YouTube など動画撮影を希望する場合は、必ず企画書を添付してください。 撮影希望日1日につき1回申し込みフォームから申請をお願いいたします。 撮影は可能な限り平日（月～金）の午前中で終了できるようにスケジュールを組んでください。 テレビ撮影やタレント・モデルを起用しての撮影の場合は、企画段階で広報担当者まで一度ご相談いただけますようお願い申し上げます。 個々のショップの中に立ち入っての撮影を希望される場合でも最初に PR 事務局宛に「敷地内撮影申込書フォーム」よりご連絡ください。 企画書を確認後、希望するショップの担当窓口(プレス・広報・店長)をご案内します。 入館退館の際は従業員用通用口（道玄坂沿い）からの入退館をお願いいたします。 1階エントランス付近での撮影や取材は店頭スペース「109イベントスペース」でイベントを実施していない時に限ります。 イベントのスケジュールは [こちら](https://shibuya109square.com/) からご確認ください。 SHIBUYA109 PR 事務局より撮影日前日までに確認のご連絡を差し上げます。 担当は曜日によって異なりますので、最初に問い合わせを入れた担当とは別の者から連絡を差し上げる場合もございます。 申込書には必ず撮影作業責任者の携帯番号をご記入ください。 撮影当日、SHIBUYA109 1階にある「防災センター」にて受付をお願いいたします。 受付時に敷地内撮影用プレスパスシールをお渡しいたします。撮影日・媒体名を受付でご記入いただき、衣服の見える場所へ貼っていただき、 取材撮影を行っていただくようお願いいたします。 ＜ご注意＞ 取材・撮影希望時間が営業時間外（午前10時前および午後9時以降）になる場合は、別途 PR 事務局担当者までお早目にご相談ください。 ※状況により営業時間を変更している場合がございます。SHIBUYA109トップページをご確認ください。 【お問い合わせ・お申し込み】 SHIBUYA109 PR事務局：㈱喜多ピーアール 広報担当：大谷 / 喜多 TEL：03-5771-5334 / FAX：03-5771-5335 Mail： [109@kita-pr.co.jp](mailto:109@kita-pr.co.jp) ご利用上の注意 以下のルールを順守いただけない場合は、撮影中止とさせていただきます。ご理解・ご協力のほどよろしくお願い申し上げます。 基本注意事項 お客様の迷惑にならないよう注意して撮影を進めてください。 キャストの方以外は全員、受付時にお渡しする撮影用プレスパスシールを必ず目立つ位置に着けてください。 フロア間の移動は、バックヤード内従業員用エレベーターをご使用ください。 機材や荷物を共用部に置かないでください。 撮影場所の近辺にあるショップの入り口や、ディスプレイの前はふさがないようにしてカメラやスタッフを配置してください。

citations.title: What Does Copyright Protect? (FAQ) | U.S. Copyright Office
excerpts: What Does Copyright Protect? **What does copyright protect?** Copyright, a form of intellectual property law, protects original works of authorship including literary, dramatic, musical, and artistic works, such as poetry, novels, movies, songs, computer software, and architecture. ... **Can I copyright my website?** The original authorship appearing on a website may be protected by copyright. This includes writings, artwork, photographs, and other forms of authorship protected by copyright. ... No one can lawfully use your photo of your sighting, although someone else may file his own photo of his sighting. Copyright law protects the original photograph, not the subject of the photograph. **Does copyright protect architecture?** Yes. Architectural works became subject to copyright protection on December 1, 1990. The copyright law defines “architectural work” as “the design of a building embodied in any tangible medium of expression, including a building, architectural plans, or drawings.” Copyright protection extends to any architectural work created on or after December 1, 1990. Also, any architectural works that were unconstructed and embodied in unpublished plans or drawings on that date and were constructed by December 31, 2002, are eligible for protection. excerpts: このページの先頭です このページの本文へ移動 サイトメニューここまで 警視庁 サイトマップ メニュー |  | × | トップページ 手続き 交通に関するもの 道路使用許可申請手続きについて 本文ここから ... 道路使用許可申請手続きについて 概要 道路を工事やイベントなど、通行以外の目的でやむを得ず使用する場合は、その場所を管轄する警察署長による道路使用許可が必要です。 ただし、道路交通法第76条により禁止されている行為は許可できません。 新規ウィンドウで開きます。 [道路使用許可申請手続き(警察庁)（外部サイト）](https://www.npa.go.jp/bureau/traffic/seibi2/shinsei-todokede/dourosiyoukyoka/dourosiyoukyoka.html) ... 道路使用許可の対象となる行為 道路において工事もしくは作業を行う場合（1号） 作業の例：クレーンを使用した資材搬出入、コンクリート打設 など 道路に石碑、広告板、アーチ等の工作物を設置する場合（2号） 工作物の例：掲示板、記念碑 など (注記)道路管理者の「道路占用許可」もあわせて必要となります。 ... 道路において祭礼行事、ロケーション等、一般交通に著しい影響を及ぼす行為を行う場合（4号） 東京都内では下記の行為を行うにあたり、一般交通に著しい影響を及ぼす場合に道路使用許可が必要となります。 祭礼行事、路上競技会、仮装行列、パレード等 著しく人目をひく装飾車 ロケーション、撮影会等 拡声器等を備え付けた車両等による放送宣伝 道路上で人寄せをする行為 消防、水防、避難、救護その他の訓練 募金、署名活動、物の販売、交付 自動運転等の実証実験 など ... 申請に必要な書類 工事･作業の場合 工事概要 現場案内図（工事・作業実施場所周辺の見取図） 緊急時の連絡先 道路使用状況図（作業帯図） 交通量調査結果           など (注記)工事・作業の内容により上記全てが必要とは限りませんので、詳細は申請先の警察署にお問合せください。 工作物の場合 現場案内図（工作物の設置場所周辺の見取図） 設置する工作物の設計図（寸法等記載のもの） など 露店等の場合 現場案内図（露店等の設置場所周辺の見取図） 設置する露店等の設計図（寸法等記載のもの） など ... 注意事項 原則として、1行為につき1申請です。 あらかじめ、道路使用の場所・区間を管轄する警察署を確認の上申請してください。 道路使用許可申請以外の申請が含まれる場合は、別途申請してください。 パーキングメーター休止・撤去申請 通行禁止道路通行許可申請 制限外等許可申請          など 広範囲に及ぶ工事、国道、都道、高速道路における工事、通行止めにして行われるイベントなど、交通への影響が大きくなることが予想されるものは、事前協議が必要となる場合がありますので、申請する前に管轄警察署に相談してください。

entries.outreach_draft:
To whom it may concern,

We are writing on behalf of the production 'Shibuya Scramble Crossing' to request a location filming agreement for the use of footage captured at the Shibuya Scramble Crossing.

The material appears from approximately 0:00:00 to 0:01:00, for a duration of 1 minute. The scene is a point-of-view shot from a motorcycle stopped at the Shibuya Scramble Crossing in Tokyo, Japan, featuring various distinctive buildings and billboards.

We are seeking rights for worldwide, all media, in perpetuity.

We are currently seeking clarity on the appropriate entity to grant this agreement. Our research indicates that the current registered title holder and trust structure for each QFRONT condominium interest were not fully identified. While TOKYU REIT publicly confirms land ownership and building compartmentalized ownership, its 2003 filing identifies a Mitsubishi Trust Bank trustee and a predecessor asset-funding seller. Additionally, the legal owner of the SHIBUYA109/道玄坂共同ビル real estate was not established from the available records; SHIBUYA109 Entertainment is confirmed as operator and brand company, not conclusively as the building owner. We would appreciate any guidance you can offer regarding the correct party or parties to approach for this location filming agreement.

Please confirm if you are the appropriate party to grant this agreement. We also request information regarding any associated fees or restrictions that may apply to this usage.

item.title: Yakult
item.description: The Yakult logo is displayed prominently on a large digital billboard.
item.evidence: A large billboard in the upper left of the frame features the red Yakult logo on a white background.

holders.name: Yakult Honsha Co., Ltd.
holders.contact: Yakult Honsha corporate office; published telephone +81-3-6625-8960
holders.notes: The official terms state that trademarks displayed on the Yakult website belong to Yakult Honsha or authorized rights holders and may not be used without permission. This is the principal party for worldwide trademark approval, including the featured Yakult logo.

holders.name: Yakult U.S.A. Inc.
holders.contact: Yakult U.S.A. Inc.; contact form; 714-434-6500; 833-434-6500; yakult@yakultusa.com
holders.notes: Yakult U.S.A. Inc. states that it supports Yakult's business in the United States and Canada. It is the appropriate local intake/contact point, but the available evidence does not establish authority to grant worldwide rights.

finding.public_domain_rationale: The depicted material is a live brand identifier rather than an out-of-copyright creative work. The U.S. YAKULT registration identified in the records is active and renewed, with Kabushiki Kaisha Yakult Honsha listed as owner. Yakult's own terms also state that its trademarks may not be used without permission. Copyright status of the exact logo artwork was not separately established, but trademark clearance remains necessary for this prominent, featured depiction.
finding.territory_notes: Yakult Honsha Co., Ltd. is the global brand owner identified in the available records. Yakult U.S.A. Inc. supports the brand in the United States and Canada, so a worldwide film clearance should be referred to Yakult Honsha and coordinated with relevant local Yakult operating companies. Approval is not automatically transferable between territories.
finding.licensing_precedent: Yakult publicly announced a product placement in Marvel's Ant-Man in July 2015. The announcement states that Yakult appears in scenes approximately 35 minutes into the film and that the film was produced by Marvel Studios under The Walt Disney Company and intended for worldwide release. The announcement discloses no placement fee or other financial terms. It also describes tie-in television commercials in the United States, Hong Kong, and Australia.
unresolved: The exact registration record for the specific red Yakult logo shown on the billboard was not identified; the located U.S. record confirms an active YAKULT word-and-design registration but does not conclusively match the depicted artwork.
No publicly identified Yakult entertainment-licensing department, standard application form, or named film-and-television approval executive was found.

The internal authority or contractual relationship by which Yakult U.S.A. Inc. can approve worldwide use was not established; its public description only confirms support for the United States and Canada.
No publicly disclosed fee, rate card, or financial terms for Yakult's film or television placements were found.

basis.reasoning: The U.S. trademark record identifies YAKULT as a live, registered and renewed mark owned by Kabushiki Kaisha Yakult Honsha. That supports treating the featured trademark as not public-domain material for clearance purposes.

excerpts: July 2015 Yakult Product Placement in Marvel’s Ant-Man Yakult Honsha Co., Ltd. finding.public_domain_rationale: This is a trademark-clearance matter rather than a conventional copyright license. Mercedes-Benz states that its star, brand, model name plates, logos and emblems are protected by trademark law and that its digital materials grant no license. The current three-pointed-star trademark was created in 1925, but trademark rights do not expire merely because an image is old or potentially uncopyrightable. The exact copyright status of the particular logo rendering and the exact GLC 350d designation was not established, so public-domain status should not be relied upon for the proposed featured commercial depiction.
finding.territory_notes: The Mercedes-Benz trademark portfolio is controlled at group level, while Mercedes-Benz USA handles distribution, marketing, customer service and financial services for Mercedes-Benz products in the United States. For the proposed worldwide, all-media, in-perpetuity use, obtain approval covering both the U.S. and non-U.S. territories; a U.S. approval should not be assumed to grant worldwide rights.
finding.licensing_precedent: Mercedes-Benz publicly announced a collaboration with Sony Pictures Animation’s film “GOAT,” including prominent in-film placement of Mercedes-Benz vehicles and associated theatrical, television, SVOD, digital and cinema advertising. The announcement confirms that Mercedes-Benz does approve prominent entertainment integrations, but it does not disclose the fee, approval workflow, or terms applicable to “Shibuya Scramble Crossing”.
unresolved: The exact current USPTO registration and ownership record for the three-pointed-star design as depicted was not identified in the available public record.

The exact registration and proprietor record for the combined “GLC 350d” model designation was not identified; the available evidence establishes group ownership of Mercedes-Benz marks and model name plates generally, not this exact designation.
No publicly identified Mercedes-Benz department or named representative specifically dedicated to film-and-television trademark approvals was found.
No publicly disclosed standard fee schedule or rate card for entertainment use was found.
Any required approval from the vehicle owner, local distributor, production partner, or other territorial Mercedes-Benz affiliate for the particular physical vehicle remains unverified.

Because the requested asset is a trademark and the exact rendering’s copyright status was not established, the appropriate conclusion is unclear rather than yes.

finding.public_domain_rationale: The Toyota logo is a trademark and brand asset, not a copyright work that becomes public domain merely because its design dates from 1937. Toyota states that the mark was registered as a trademark in April 1937 and that the current emblem was introduced in 1989. Toyota's U.S. terms also state that Toyota or its affiliates own or have rights in the trademarks and prohibit other trademark use without written approval. The visible taxi logo should therefore be treated as protected trademark property, notwithstanding possible legal defenses for incidental, non-endorsing depiction.

You get to use a brand’s product at no cost, and the brand gets exposure from being in your movie. While hefty checks are nice, don’t write off the benefits of complimentary usage for product placement in movies. Consider all the many items of clothing, furniture, or even notable locales that can come at no cost if you successfully pitch the brand. ... However, there’s a fine line to walk with product placement, brand recognition, and audience reaction. In fact, _Wayne’s World_ notoriously lampoons the [excessive usage](https://blog.hollywoodbranded.com/infographic-the-crazy-product-placement-world-of-waynes-world) of product placement in its own movie. Wayne gives a wink and nod to his audience, all while trotting out Pizza Put, Doritos, Reebok, Nuprin, and Pepsi within a minute of screentime. Audiences are in on the joke with Wayne and Garth. But if you’re asking viewers to take seriously a film where you’re showcasing brands only because you got their products for free, those viewers may come to negatively regard another product – yours. ... With that disclaimer in mind, many brands are happy to provide free products if you can demonstrate what kind of positive exposure they’ll receive for it. That might mean providing a treatment, pitch deck, storyboards, or all of the above to highlight how their products or services will be included in your movie. ... Also, be reasonable about your ask. You get to use a brand’s product at no cost, and the brand gets exposure from being in your movie. While hefty checks are nice, don’t write off the benefits of complimentary usage for product placement in movies. Consider all the many items of clothing, furniture, or even notable locales that can come at no cost if you successfully pitch the brand. ... However, there’s a fine line to walk with product placement, brand recognition, and audience reaction. In fact, _Wayne’s World_ notoriously lampoons the [excessive usage](https://blog.hollywoodbranded.com/infographic-the-crazy-product-placement-world-of-waynes-world) of product placement in its own movie. Wayne gives a wink and nod to his audience, all while trotting out Pizza Put, Doritos, Reebok, Nuprin, and Pepsi within a minute of screentime. Audiences are in on the joke with Wayne and Garth. But if you’re asking viewers to take seriously a film where you’re showcasing brands only because you got their products for free, those viewers may come to negatively regard another product – yours. ... With that disclaimer in mind, many brands are happy to provide free products if you can demonstrate what kind of positive exposure they’ll receive for it. That might mean providing a treatment, pitch deck, storyboards, or all of the above to highlight how their products or services will be included in your movie. ... Also, be reasonable about your ask. A global brand like Doritos may not mind shipping a dozen boxes of product for your project. But are you asking a small, local business owner for the same? Then they might turn you down.

holders.name: Unidentified advertisers, sign designers, printers, landlords, and outdoor-media operators for the remaining Japanese signs
holders.contact: Not identified from the supplied footage
holders.notes: The description says that numerous other signs are legible, but does not provide a complete readable inventory. Each sign must be matched to its advertiser and, where applicable, its creative owner and display-site operator.

finding.public_domain_rationale: The material cannot be classified as public domain on the present record. Under U.S. guidance, business names, slogans, short phrases, typeface, and ordinary lettering generally are not copyrightable, but sufficiently creative logo artwork may be protected. The first-publication/creation dates and authorship for the specific signs are unknown; U.S. copyright duration depends on those facts. Japan's incidental-inclusion rule may permit use of a work that is difficult to separate from the principal filmed subject and is only a light/background component, but that is a limitation on infringement rather than a finding that the sign is public domain.
finding.territory_notes: The identifiable brands are Japanese rights holders, but no evidence establishes that either controls worldwide rights in every sign design or advertising execution. For a worldwide, all-media, in-perpetuity release, clearance should cover each identifiable brand, the underlying logo artwork, any campaign creative, and any relevant billboard/OOH operator. Japan's incidental-inclusion rules may reduce copyright risk for genuinely background signage, but they do not automatically resolve trademark, reputation, contractual, or non-Japanese issues.
finding.licensing_precedent: No documented film or television license specific to the pictured Aiful or Acom signs, and no reported fee for these signs, was identified. General licensing guidance states that fees vary with media, term, and territory and are ordinarily quoted or negotiated; some brand-film partnerships involve no fee, but that is not a dependable benchmark for a worldwide perpetual clearance of background signage.
unresolved: The footage does not provide a complete inventory of the signs; only Aiful and Acom are specifically identifiable from the supplied description, while other legible businesses remain unidentified.

Ownership of the creative artwork in each sign has not been established. Aiful or Acom may own the brand and trademark, but an advertising agency, photographer, designer, printer, landlord, or outdoor-media operator may own or control particular artwork or display rights.

The first-publication or installation date, campaign/version, and exact location of each sign are unknown, so the U.S. copyright term and whether an older or replaced creative is shown cannot be determined.
It has not been established whether the camera merely captured the signs incidentally or deliberately framed/held on them. That distinction is material under Japan's incidental-inclusion analysis.
A worldwide all-media perpetual release, if required by the distributor or E&O insurer, has not been obtained from the identified companies or any other relevant rights holders.

basis.reasoning: The U.S. Copyright Office states that names, slogans, short phrases, and logos are generally not protected as such, while artistic logo artwork may qualify for copyright. It also states that duration depends on publication, creation, authorship, and work category. Those facts are unavailable for the individual signs, so public-domain status is unclear rather than yes.

citations.title: How Long Does Copyright Protection Last? (FAQ) | U.S. Copyright Office
excerpts: How Long Does Copyright Protection Last? **How long does a copyright last?** The term of copyright for a particular work depends on several factors, including whether it has been published, and, if so, the date of first publication. As a general rule, for works created after January 1, 1978, copyright protection lasts for the life of the author plus an additional 70 years. For an anonymous work, a pseudonymous work, or a work made for hire, the copyright endures for a term of 95 years from the year of its first publication or a term of 120 years from the year of its creation, whichever expires first.

basis.reasoning: The Japanese Agency for Cultural Affairs describes an incidental-inclusion rule that can permit use of an incidental work in the audiovisual work, subject to an unreasonable-harm proviso. WIPO explains that clearance depends on the laws where rights are exploited and that chain of title must be documented. excerpts: （付随対象著作物の利用） 第30条の2 写真の撮影，録音又は録画（以下この項において「写真の撮影等」という。）の方法によつて著作物を創作するに当たつて，当該著作物（以下この条において「写真等著作物」という。）に係る写真の撮影等の対象とする事物又は音から分離することが困難であるため付随して対象となる事物又は音に係る他の著作物（当該写真等著作物における軽微な構成部分となるものに限る。以下この条において「付随対象著作物」という。）は，当該創作に伴つて複製又は翻案することができる。ただし，当該付随対象著作物の種類及び用途並びに当該複製又は翻案の態様に照らし著作権者の利益を不当に害することとなる場合は，この限りでない。 2 前項の規定により複製又は翻案された付随対象著作物は，同項に規定する写真等著作物の利用に伴つて利用することができる。ただし，当該付随対象著作物の種類及び用途並びに当該利用の態様に照らし著作権者の利益を不当に害することとなる場合は，この限りでない。 著作物の創作や利用に際しては，例えば，写真撮影やビデオ収録の際，背景に著作物であるキャラクターが写り込んでしまうといったことや，キャラクターが写り込んだ写真等をブログ等に掲載するといったことが行われています。こうした写り込んでしまった著作物の利用は，通常著作権者の利益を不当に害するものではありませんが，著作権侵害に問われるおそれがありました。 このため，写真の撮影等の方法によって著作物を創作するに当たって，当該著作物（写真等著作物）に係る撮影等の対象とする事物等から分離することが困難であるため付随して対象となる事物等に係る他の著作物（付随対象著作物）は，当該創作に伴って複製又は翻案することが侵害行為に当たらないことを明確にしました。（第1項） また，複製又は翻案された付随対象著作物は，写真等著作物の利用に伴って利用することが侵害行為に当たらないことを明確にしました。（第2項） 本条第1項で，「分離することが困難である」とあるのは，ある著作物（写真等著作物）を創作する際に，創作時の状況に照らして，付随して対象となった他の著作物（付随対象著作物）を除いて創作することが，社会通念上困難であると客観的に認められることをいいます。 また，「当該写真等著作物における軽微な構成部分となるものに限る」とありますが，「軽微な構成部分」であるか否かは，著作物の種類等に照らし，個別の事案に応じて判断されるものであり，予め定量的な割合が決まっているものではありません。 ... 本条第2項では，「利用することができる」と規定しているため，「利用」全般が著作権者の許諾を得ることなく行うことができ，複製，上映，演奏，公衆送信，譲渡など全ての支分権に該当する行為が想定されています。 なお，本条第1項の「付随対象著作物」は，写真の撮影等の対象とする事物等から分離することが困難であるため付随して対象となるものです。この「付随対象著作物」については，撮影後には画像処理等により「付随対象著作物」を消去することが可能な場合が考えられますが，本条第2項では条文上「分離することが困難であること」を要件としておらず，「付随対象著作物」を「写真等著作物」から分離することが可能であっても，著作権者の許諾を得ることなく利用することができます。 また，同項においても，本条第1項と同様のただし書が規定されています。 本条の対象となる著作物の利用行為としては，以下のような例が考えられます。（ただし，本条の対象となるかどうかについては，最終的には，個別具体の事例に応じ，司法の場で判断されることになります。以下，他の条文の対象となる著作物の利用行為の例についても同様です。） ...

citations.title: 2 Rights Clearance From Idea To Distribution
excerpts: 2 Rights Clearance: from idea to distribution Understanding rights clearance What is rights clearance? Audiovisual productions incorporate, adapt and use vast quantities of preexisting material that is protected by various categories of rights. In most cases, the producer must obtain permission before using those rights. A right is “cleared” when an object or a person that integrates the project (a music, a painting, a product, a magazine, the photograph of someone, etc.) is identified, evaluated according to the circumstances of the use and the rights required for a lawful use also identified. ... Chain-of-title is the unbroken record of ownership of the copyright and other legal rights in the film property. The chain-of-title is a condition for the circulation of the film in the market and the producer is required by all those involved in the exploitation of the content to expressly assert it for distributors, sales agents and so on. ... Why is rights clearance important? The decision whether a film is considered to be infringing someone’s rights is taken considering the laws where that right was exploited, for example when a film or series will reach the audiences (with some exceptions that are better analyzed case-by-case by an entertainment lawyer). Although national laws differ, there is an overall similarity in a number of issues specially regarding a minimum level of protection.

citations.title: 著作権についての取り組み | 日本映画・テレビ 美術監督協会
excerpts: 番組でうさぎのマスコットをデザインして作ったんですが、そのマスコットを商品化したりLINEスタンプとして販売したいと打診がありました。 その場合、著作権使用料として何％かの報酬を請求できますか？ 大前提として、うさぎのマスコットのデザインは、独立した美術の著作物ということになり、その著作者・著作権者は、その作成者になる。契約により映画製作者に著作権が譲渡されていない場合には、商品化などの利用についての権限まで映画製作者等に譲渡されているとはいえないと考える。 従って、番組の宣伝などとは別個の商品化利用については、別途、製作会社側等と再度利用についての契約を結ぶことになる。 著作権使用料の相場については、守秘義務があるので公にされていないため確かな事は言えませんが、ミッキーマウスなどの有名なキャラクターだと7%～10%かもしれませんが、相場としては、商品販売価格の3～5％ぐらいではないでしょうか？ 私的には、5%だと少々高いなという感覚です。LINEスタンプのような場合には、あまり製作原価がかからないので、著作権使用料も高くなったりすると思います。 こちらが著作権使用料を丸々もらうということもあり得ない話ではありますが、元々番組があって生まれたキャラクターで、製作会社に料金の徴収などの事務処理などをしてもらうことがあったりするので、この場合は、製作会社側が窓口となり使用料を折半するという形も多く取られているのではないかと思います。 映り込みの話で、ロケなどの場合はどうしても映ってしまいますが、著作権侵害になりますか？ ケースバイケースですが、1/3でも半分映っても十分、著作物を利用していることになります。 複製権侵害を考えるときに、例えば、大きな絵画の中の一部に描かれている蝶々をワンポイントでＴシャツにプリントした場合、それは、絵画の中に占める割合にかかわらず著作権侵害になります。 但し、ロケなどでどうしても映ってしまう場合は、現行法上は映り込み（付随対象著作物の利用。30条の2）として侵害にはなりません。 「映り込み」と「映し込み（敢えて映した）」は区別が難しいケースがたくさんあります。 たまたま絵画の前に人が立っていてその人が映るのは「写り込み」ですが、敢えて絵画の前に立ってもらって撮影したら「映し込み」です。 ただし、映像それ自体からは判別できないことも多いと思います。 この映り込みの規定は、26年改正で設けられた規定なので、今までは映り込みとなかなか言えなかったのですが、今は言えるようになったという事です。 なお、建物にある壁画や屋外に設置された彫刻は、恒常的に設置された美術の著作物ということになるので、映したとしても著作権侵害にはなりません。 映画の場合の私たち美術監督の著作権に関しては、映画の中で、自由に包括的に追加使用料なしで使える権利を許諾してください。という話なので、映画が10年ぶりにリバイバルで上映されてもずっと使い続けられる契約として、特に期限も決められているわけではありません。 ただし、映画と切り離したところで使われるのは許諾の範囲を超えた利用として著作権侵害になります。 契約書は常に作るようにしなければなりませんか？ 実務の慣行としてきちんとした契約書を作らないことが多い、多かったと想像しています。 私は、無理に契約書を作成しなくとも、後日になっても合意の内容がはっきりしているような記録を残しておけばよいと考えています。契約書を交わさないような仕事を頼まれた場合は、メールでポイント（仕事の内容、納期、金額など）を確認しておくことをお勧めします。 電話や口頭でやりとりした場合であれば、お礼を兼ねてその内容を書いてメールしておくだけで全然違います。さらに担当者だけではなくその上司や関係者など複数の人にc.c.で送るとなおよいと思います。 メールは、裁判などでは改竄できるので証拠能力が弱いとは言われてますが、意図的な改竄をして誤魔化すという人は、業界からはじかれてしまうのでまずいないと思います。口約束だけだと、勘違いをしたり、約束の内容が曖昧だったりしてトラブルになるので、そのようなことを防ぐには、お礼も兼ねたメールを送って内容を確認しておくのはオススメの方法だと思っています。 これは、許諾を取るなどの時も同じで、許諾してくれた担当者と権利者本人にメールを送っておくと後々のトラブルを大きく減らせます。

citations.title: How Long Does Copyright Protection Last? (FAQ) | U.S. Copyright Office
excerpts: How Long Does Copyright Protection Last? **How long does a copyright last?** The term of copyright for a particular work depends on several factors, including whether it has been published, and, if so, the date of first publication. As a general rule, for works created after January 1, 1978, copyright protection lasts for the life of the author plus an additional 70 years. For an anonymous work, a pseudonymous work, or a work made for hire, the copyright endures for a term of 95 years from the year of its first publication or a term of 120 years from the year of its creation, whichever expires first.

excerpts: （付随対象著作物の利用） 第30条の2 写真の撮影，録音又は録画（以下この項において「写真の撮影等」という。）の方法によつて著作物を創作するに当たつて，当該著作物（以下この条において「写真等著作物」という。）に係る写真の撮影等の対象とする事物又は音から分離することが困難であるため付随して対象となる事物又は音に係る他の著作物（当該写真等著作物における軽微な構成部分となるものに限る。以下この条において「付随対象著作物」という。）は，当該創作に伴つて複製又は翻案することができる。ただし，当該付随対象著作物の種類及び用途並びに当該複製又は翻案の態様に照らし著作権者の利益を不当に害することとなる場合は，この限りでない。 2 前項の規定により複製又は翻案された付随対象著作物は，同項に規定する写真等著作物の利用に伴つて利用することができる。ただし，当該付随対象著作物の種類及び用途並びに当該利用の態様に照らし著作権者の利益を不当に害することとなる場合は，この限りでない。 著作物の創作や利用に際しては，例えば，写真撮影やビデオ収録の際，背景に著作物であるキャラクターが写り込んでしまうといったことや，キャラクターが写り込んだ写真等をブログ等に掲載するといったことが行われています。こうした写り込んでしまった著作物の利用は，通常著作権者の利益を不当に害するものではありませんが，著作権侵害に問われるおそれがありました。 このため，写真の撮影等の方法によって著作物を創作するに当たって，当該著作物（写真等著作物）に係る撮影等の対象とする事物等から分離することが困難であるため付随して対象となる事物等に係る他の著作物（付随対象著作物）は，当該創作に伴って複製又は翻案することが侵害行為に当たらないことを明確にしました。（第1項） また，複製又は翻案された付随対象著作物は，写真等著作物の利用に伴って利用することが侵害行為に当たらないことを明確にしました。（第2項） 本条第1項で，「分離することが困難である」とあるのは，ある著作物（写真等著作物）を創作する際に，創作時の状況に照らして，付随して対象となった他の著作物（付随対象著作物）を除いて創作することが，社会通念上困難であると客観的に認められることをいいます。 また，「当該写真等著作物における軽微な構成部分となるものに限る」とありますが，「軽微な構成部分」であるか否かは，著作物の種類等に照らし，個別の事案に応じて判断されるものであり，予め定量的な割合が決まっているものではありません。 ... 本条第2項では，「利用することができる」と規定しているため，「利用」全般が著作権者の許諾を得ることなく行うことができ，複製，上映，演奏，公衆送信，譲渡など全ての支分権に該当する行為が想定されています。 なお，本条第1項の「付随対象著作物」は，写真の撮影等の対象とする事物等から分離することが困難であるため付随して対象となるものです。この「付随対象著作物」については，撮影後には画像処理等により「付随対象著作物」を消去することが可能な場合が考えられますが，本条第2項では条文上「分離することが困難であること」を要件としておらず，「付随対象著作物」を「写真等著作物」から分離することが可能であっても，著作権者の許諾を得ることなく利用することができます。 また，同項においても，本条第1項と同様のただし書が規定されています。 本条の対象となる著作物の利用行為としては，以下のような例が考えられます。（ただし，本条の対象となるかどうかについては，最終的には，個別具体の事例に応じ，司法の場で判断されることになります。以下，他の条文の対象となる著作物の利用行為の例についても同様です。） ...

citations.title: 著作権についての取り組み | 日本映画・テレビ 美術監督協会
excerpts: 番組でうさぎのマスコットをデザインして作ったんですが、そのマスコットを商品化したりLINEスタンプとして販売したいと打診がありました。 その場合、著作権使用料として何％かの報酬を請求できますか？ 大前提として、うさぎのマスコットのデザインは、独立した美術の著作物ということになり、その著作者・著作権者は、その作成者になる。契約により映画製作者に著作権が譲渡されていない場合には、商品化などの利用についての権限まで映画製作者等に譲渡されているとはいえないと考える。 従って、番組の宣伝などとは別個の商品化利用については、別途、製作会社側等と再度利用についての契約を結ぶことになる。 著作権使用料の相場については、守秘義務があるので公にされていないため確かな事は言えませんが、ミッキーマウスなどの有名なキャラクターだと7%～10%かもしれませんが、相場としては、商品販売価格の3～5％ぐらいではないでしょうか？ 私的には、5%だと少々高いなという感覚です。LINEスタンプのような場合には、あまり製作原価がかからないので、著作権使用料も高くなったりすると思います。 こちらが著作権使用料を丸々もらうということもあり得ない話ではありますが、元々番組があって生まれたキャラクターで、製作会社に料金の徴収などの事務処理などをしてもらうことがあったりするので、この場合は、製作会社側が窓口となり使用料を折半するという形も多く取られているのではないかと思います。 映り込みの話で、ロケなどの場合はどうしても映ってしまいますが、著作権侵害になりますか？ ケースバイケースですが、1/3でも半分映っても十分、著作物を利用していることになります。 複製権侵害を考えるときに、例えば、大きな絵画の中の一部に描かれている蝶々をワンポイントでＴシャツにプリントした場合、それは、絵画の中に占める割合にかかわらず著作権侵害になります。 但し、ロケなどでどうしても映ってしまう場合は、現行法上は映り込み（付随対象著作物の利用。30条の2）として侵害にはなりません。 「映り込み」と「映し込み（敢えて映した）」は区別が難しいケースがたくさんあります。 たまたま絵画の前に人が立っていてその人が映るのは「写り込み」ですが、敢えて絵画の前に立ってもらって撮影したら「映し込み」です。 ただし、映像それ自体からは判別できないことも多いと思います。 この映り込みの規定は、26年改正で設けられた規定なので、今までは映り込みとなかなか言えなかったのですが、今は言えるようになったという事です。 なお、建物にある壁画や屋外に設置された彫刻は、恒常的に設置された美術の著作物ということになるので、映したとしても著作権侵害にはなりません。 映画の場合の私たち美術監督の著作権に関しては、映画の中で、自由に包括的に追加使用料なしで使える権利を許諾してください。という話なので、映画が10年ぶりにリバイバルで上映されてもずっと使い続けられる契約として、特に期限も決められているわけではありません。 ただし、映画と切り離したところで使われるのは許諾の範囲を超えた利用として著作権侵害になります。 契約書は常に作るようにしなければなりませんか？ 実務の慣行としてきちんとした契約書を作らないことが多い、多かったと想像しています。 私は、無理に契約書を作成しなくとも、後日になっても合意の内容がはっきりしているような記録を残しておけばよいと考えています。契約書を交わさないような仕事を頼まれた場合は、メールでポイント（仕事の内容、納期、金額など）を確認しておくことをお勧めします。 電話や口頭でやりとりした場合であれば、お礼を兼ねてその内容を書いてメールしておくだけで全然違います。さらに担当者だけではなくその上司や関係者など複数の人にc.c.で送るとなおよいと思います。 メールは、裁判などでは改竄できるので証拠能力が弱いとは言われてますが、意図的な改竄をして誤魔化すという人は、業界からはじかれてしまうのでまずいないと思います。口約束だけだと、勘違いをしたり、約束の内容が曖昧だったりしてトラブルになるので、そのようなことを防ぐには、お礼も兼ねたメールを送って内容を確認しておくのはオススメの方法だと思っています。 これは、許諾を取るなどの時も同じで、許諾してくれた担当者と権利者本人にメールを送っておくと後々のトラブルを大きく減らせます。

citations.title: bunka.go.jp
excerpts: （付随対象著作物の利用） 第30条の2 写真の撮影，録音又は録画（以下この項において「写真の撮影等」という。）の方法によつて著作物を創作するに当たつて，当該著作物（以下この条において「写真等著作物」という。）に係る写真の撮影等の対象とする事物又は音から分離することが困難であるため付随して対象となる事物又は音に係る他の著作物（当該写真等著作物における軽微な構成部分となるものに限る。以下この条において「付随対象著作物」という。）は，当該創作に伴つて複製又は翻案することができる。ただし，当該付随対象著作物の種類及び用途並びに当該複製又は翻案の態様に照らし著作権者の利益を不当に害することとなる場合は，この限りでない。 2 前項の規定により複製又は翻案された付随対象著作物は，同項に規定する写真等著作物の利用に伴つて利用することができる。ただし，当該付随対象著作物の種類及び用途並びに当該利用の態様に照らし著作権者の利益を不当に害することとなる場合は，この限りでない。 著作物の創作や利用に際しては，例えば，写真撮影やビデオ収録の際，背景に著作物であるキャラクターが写り込んでしまうといったことや，キャラクターが写り込んだ写真等をブログ等に掲載するといったことが行われています。こうした写り込んでしまった著作物の利用は，通常著作権者の利益を不当に害するものではありませんが，著作権侵害に問われるおそれがありました。 このため，写真の撮影等の方法によって著作物を創作するに当たって，当該著作物（写真等著作物）に係る撮影等の対象とする事物等から分離することが困難であるため付随して対象となる事物等に係る他の著作物（付随対象著作物）は，当該創作に伴って複製又は翻案することが侵害行為に当たらないことを明確にしました。（第1項） また，複製又は翻案された付随対象著作物は，写真等著作物の利用に伴って利用することが侵害行為に当たらないことを明確にしました。（第2項） 本条第1項で，「分離することが困難である」とあるのは，ある著作物（写真等著作物）を創作する際に，創作時の状況に照らして，付随して対象となった他の著作物（付随対象著作物）を除いて創作することが，社会通念上困難であると客観的に認められることをいいます。 また，「当該写真等著作物における軽微な構成部分となるものに限る」とありますが，「軽微な構成部分」であるか否かは，著作物の種類等に照らし，個別の事案に応じて判断されるものであり，予め定量的な割合が決まっているものではありません。

finding.public_domain_rationale: The Tokyo 2020 Olympic and Paralympic emblems were publicly launched on 24 July 2015. The official Brand Protection Guidelines state that the marks and related intellectual property are protected by trademark, unfair-competition, and copyright laws, and that Olympic-property rights belong exclusively to the IOC. The U.S. TOKYO 2020 mark remains recorded as registered to the USOPC. Nothing in the evidence indicates a dedication to the public domain or expiration of the relevant rights; the background appearance in a film does not itself make the mark public-domain material.
finding.territory_notes: The International Olympic Committee (IOC) is the worldwide proprietor of Olympic properties, including the Tokyo 2020 Olympic emblem and associated Olympic marks. In Japan, management was entrusted to the Tokyo Organising Committee during the Games, but the Tokyo 2020 emblem was reassigned to the IOC in December 2021. In the United States, the five-ring TOKYO 2020 composite mark is registered to the United States Olympic and Paralympic Committee (USOPC). A worldwide film licence should therefore obtain IOC clearance for global Olympic-property rights and USOPC clearance for U.S. commercial use, while checking local Olympic-protection laws in other territories.
finding.licensing_precedent: No specific publicly documented film or television licence for the Tokyo 2020 trademark, and no reported fee, was located. The IOC's Olympic Television Archive Bureau publicly describes case-by-case licensing, rights clearance, and final production approvals for Olympic footage used in television and other productions. That is a relevant clearance precedent for Olympic content administration, but it is not proof of a trademark-logo licence or of a standard fee for the sticker.

Confirm whether the sticker depicts the five-ring TOKYO 2020 composite mark (including U.S. Registration No. 5,216,935) or the separate Tokyo 2020 Olympic emblem, and check whether any taxi/operator artwork rights are implicated.

A complete country-by-country trademark assignment audit for the requested worldwide licence was not located. The evidence confirms the IOC position in Japan and the USOPC position in the United States, but not every national filing or local successor record.

The Tokyo 2020 Brand Protection Guidelines identify Brandmanagement@tokyo2020.jp as the 2020 Brand Management Division contact. A current dedicated film-and-television trademark-approval desk replacing that contact is not publicly identified.

citations.title: Olympic Licensing - IOC Global Licensing Programme
excerpts: Licensing Programme Licensing Programme Through the sale of official merchandise, collectibles and souvenirs, the Olympic licensing programmes offer fans a tangible connection to the Olympic Games and the Olympic values. In addition to the licensing programmes that operate for each edition of the Olympic Games, which are managed by the local Organising Committees, as part of the Olympic Agenda 2020 initiatives the IOC has also developed a global licensing programme to strengthen and promote the Olympic brand, not only during the Olympic Games, but between the Games as well. Olympic licensing consists of three core programmes aimed at specific target groups: the Olympic Heritage Collection, the Olympic Collection and the Olympic Games Collection. To support these licensing programmes and engage fans around the world, the IOC has launched a unified online [**Olympic shop**](https://shop.olympics.com/en/) available globally (except in China), offering visitors the opportunity to purchase official Olympic branded products from the three core programmes, which are produced by licensees and suppliers appointed by the IOC and the Organising Committees of upcoming Games editions. Within China, the IOC has launched an official **[Olympic online store](http://theolympicstore.tmall.com/)** hosted on the Tmall platform of Worldwide TOP Partner Alibaba. These e-commerce solutions provide another tangible touchpoint for people to engage with the Olympic Movement and the Olympic Games. **The Olympic collection** The Olympic Collection is developed by the IOC, and aims to engage a young and active audience through unique branded products that are exclusively available online and at The Olympic Museum Shop in Lausanne, Switzerland. This includes apparel, toys and games, bags, stationery items and sports equipment. **The Olympic heritage collection** The Olympic Heritage Collection offers products featuring art and design elements from previous Games editions, such as apparel, mascots and accessories, connecting fans and connoisseurs with the rich heritage of past Olympic Games. Many of these programmes are managed by the local Organising Committees, under the direction of the IOC, and help provide part of the revenues required to stage the Games. On a global level, the IOC manages the categories of videogames, sports equipment and toys. **The Olympic and Paralympic Games Collections** The Olympic and Paralympic Games Collections celebrate each upcoming edition of the Olympic and Paralympic Games, and include branded products such as accessories, souvenirs, fan gear and apparel. These programmes are managed by the local Organising Committees, under the direction of the IOC, and help provide part of the revenues required to stage the Games. Through the sale of official products, the Olympic and Paralympic Games Collections help to promote the Games and the Olympic brand, while also sharing the culture of the host region and allowing members of the public to purchase their own piece of Olympic history.

excerpts: 取材のお申込みについて 取材ご希望の方は、下記いずれかページ内の申し込みフォームより必要事項をご記入の上送信してください。 [](https://shibuya109.jp/coverage-personal) 取材受付のご案内 敷地内で撮影を希望される方は以下の順序に従って申請をお願いいたします。 内容によってはお断りをさせていただく場合もございますので予めご了承ください。 敷地内で撮影を希望される方へ 下記をご一読の上、ページ下記にある「敷地内撮影申込書フォーム」から申請 撮影の日時・場所・内容などが決まり次第、お早目にお送りください。 受付の締め切りは撮影希望日の3日前17時まで（土日祝は日数に含まず）となります。 例)撮影日が火曜日の場合、締め切りは前週の木曜日となります。 TV 番組や YouTube など動画撮影を希望する場合は、必ず企画書を添付してください。 撮影希望日1日につき1回申し込みフォームから申請をお願いいたします。 撮影は可能な限り平日（月～金）の午前中で終了できるようにスケジュールを組んでください。 テレビ撮影やタレント・モデルを起用しての撮影の場合は、企画段階で広報担当者まで一度ご相談いただけますようお願い申し上げます。 個々のショップの中に立ち入っての撮影を希望される場合でも最初に PR 事務局宛に「敷地内撮影申込書フォーム」よりご連絡ください。 企画書を確認後、希望するショップの担当窓口(プレス・広報・店長)をご案内します。 入館退館の際は従業員用通用口（道玄坂沿い）からの入退館をお願いいたします。 1階エントランス付近での撮影や取材は店頭スペース「109イベントスペース」でイベントを実施していない時に限ります。 イベントのスケジュールは [こちら](https://shibuya109square.com/) からご確認ください。

finding.public_domain_rationale: The documented TSUTAYA logo file is described as consisting only of simple geometric shapes or text and as not meeting the threshold of originality for copyright protection. That supports public-domain treatment of the depicted logo artwork in the United States, but it does not eliminate trademark, unfair-competition, publicity, property, or other clearance issues. Public-domain artwork status is therefore not permission to use the TSUTAYA mark commercially.
finding.territory_notes: No territory split or worldwide grant is publicly documented. Culture Convenience Club is confirmed as the TSUTAYA operator, and the SHIBUYA TSUTAYA website identifies itself as a Culture Convenience Club site; however, this does not establish that it alone can clear worldwide depiction of the specific QFRONT façade signage. Building, property, franchise, or local signage rights may require separate confirmation.
finding.licensing_precedent: No publicly documented film or television licensing precedent, entertainment-use policy, or reported fee for TSUTAYA depiction was identified.
unresolved: The current trademark-register record for the exact TSUTAYA word mark and logo, including registration numbers, classes, renewal status, and any assignments, has not been established.
No dedicated film-and-television brand-approval department, licensing form, or entertainment-use policy was publicly identified; the available route is a general TSUTAYA/CCC inquiry channel.
Worldwide authority to approve depiction of the specific QFRONT façade signage has not been established.
The owner or other rights holder responsible for the QFRONT building and its exterior signage has not been identified.

excerpts: About us](https://www.uber.com/us/en/about/) [Our offerings](https://www.uber.com/us/en/about/uber-offerings/) [How Uber works](https://www.uber.com/us/en/about/how-does-uber-work/) [Sustainability](https://www.uber.com/us/en/about/sustainability/) [Newsroom](https://www.uber.com/us/en/newsroom/) [Investor relations](https://investor.uber.com/) [Blog](https://www.uber.com/us/en/blog/) * Select jurisdiction: United States Select language: English Last modified: 8/11/2026 **Uber Trademark Policy** **Notification of Trademark Infringement:** Uber Technologies, Inc. (“Uber”) respects the intellectual property rights of others and abides by local and federal laws relating thereto. It is Uber’s policy, in appropriate circumstances and at its sole discretion, to disable and/or terminate the accounts of users who repeatedly infringe or are repeatedly charged with infringing the trademarks or other intellectual property rights of others. **Trademarks** Uber respects the rights of trademark owners and may assist trademark owners with the removal of infringing content. Uber is not an arbiter of third-party disputes and recognizes that third-parties may sometimes lawfully use trademarks owned by other parties. Accordingly, we encourage parties to an infringement dispute to communicate with each other to try to find an amicable resolution to the dispute. If you believe someone is infringing your trademark, you may submit a trademark complaint to Uber at the email or land address provided below; your complaint must include the following information: **Trademark Complaint Process** 1\. Provide your name, company name, and/or relationship to the trademark owner. 2\. Identify the trademark(s) you claim is/are being infringed, including (a) the mark(s) (b) the trademark registration number(s); (c) the jurisdiction(s) in which the mark(s) is/are registered; and (d) a copy of the registration certificate(s) or other proof of ownership. 3\. Identify the material you claim is infringing your trademark(s) and information reasonably sufficient to permit us to locate the allegedly infringing material, including, at a minimum, the URL of the site(s) where such material may be found, if the material appears online, as well as the name and contact information of the alleged infringer, if available. 4\. Include a brief description of why you believe the material infringes your trademark(s) and the action(s) you would like to be taken. 5\. Provide an email address, telephone number, and mailing address at which we can contact you regarding this complaint. 6\. Include both of the following statements in the body of the Notice: “I hereby state that I am the owner (or authorized agent) of the trademark(s) that is allegedly infringed and I have a good faith belief that the disputed use of the trademark(s) is not authorized by the owner, its agent, or the law (e.g., as a fair use).” “I hereby state, under penalty of perjury, that the information in this complaint is true, complete and accurate.” 7\. Provide your full legal name and your electronic or physical signature. 8\. Deliver this Complaint with all items completed to the following email or land address: Trademark Agent c/o Uber Technologies, Inc. 1725 3rd Street San Francisco, CA 94158 takedowns [at] uber [dot] com _Upon submission of your complaint, you will receive an automatic reply that your communication has been received._ If the complaint is incomplete, you will receive a notification that identifies the missing information required for Uber to review the complaint. When your complaint is complete, Uber reserves the right to determine, in its sole discretion, that the complaint is without merit and, if so, to decline to take any further action. You will be notified of any such determination. Otherwise, Uber will forward your complaint and contact information to the allegedly infringing party, who will have 10 business days to provide a response. If no response is received within 10 business days, Uber may remove any allegedly infringing material or disable the allegedly infringing account. If a response is received, Uber will forward it to you, with a copy to the allegedly infringing party, and ask that you contact the party directly to try to amicably resolve the matter. If you and the allegedly infringing party are unable to amicably resolve the matter, Uber will engage third-party legal counsel to review the dispute and recommend which party to the dispute should prevail. Uber will inform both parties of legal counsel’s recommendation and then, absent extraordinary circumstances, take or decline to take action accordingly. _If you do not receive email communication from Uber regarding your complaint, please check your spam folder, before inquiring at takedowns@uber.com. You may also wish to add takedowns@uber.com to your spam filter’s safe list.

finding.public_domain_rationale: This is a trademark and logo-clearance matter, not a work that becomes freely usable merely because of age. Starbucks' official terms identify Starbucks, Starbucks Coffee Company, the Starbucks logo, and related graphics and logos as trademarks or registered trademarks of Starbucks Corporation and state that use requires prior written permission. The STARBUCKS COFFEE registration was filed in 1988, registered in 1989, and recorded as registered and renewed; Starbucks' official brand materials trace the logo family to 1971. The stylized logo may also raise a separate copyright question, which has not been independently resolved.
finding.territory_notes: The Starbucks marks are controlled by Starbucks Corporation, but a worldwide, all-media, perpetual grant is not automatic and must be expressly approved in writing. Japan has a local operating company, Starbucks Coffee Japan, Ltd.; coordination with the Japanese operator and separate permission for the QFRONT/location may be appropriate. No territory-specific film-clearance office or published territorial tariff was identified.
finding.licensing_precedent: No Starbucks-specific paid fee for a comparable background facade depiction was publicly documented. A 2019 Game of Thrones coffee-cup incident was widely perceived as Starbucks placement, but the cup was not actually a Starbucks cup and therefore is not a licensing precedent. Industry reporting states that Starbucks has an active product-placement program, that its scripted-content appearances are often relationship-based or unpaid, and that general film product-placement arrangements range from free loan/trade arrangements to approximately $50,000-$500,000, with million-dollar deals less common. A background facade appearance would ordinarily be toward the free or low-fee end, but worldwide, all-media, perpetual rights could be negotiated differently.
unresolved: The exact registration records for the combined green circular logo and Starbucks Coffee wordmark visible on the QFRONT facade have not been fully mapped; the identified STARBUCKS COFFEE registration is one relevant registration, not necessarily the complete logo portfolio.

Starbucks has not publicly identified a dedicated film-and-television clearance executive or published entertainment-licensing tariff. The official partnerships inbox is an intake route, but the final approving department or signatory is not named publicly.
Permission from the QFRONT building owner, landlord, operator, or relevant Japanese location-rights holder has not been established; trademark permission alone may not clear the filmed facade.
The relationship between Starbucks Corporation's worldwide trademark rights and any Japan-specific license or sublicensing arrangements has not been documented for this particular depiction.

basis.reasoning: Starbucks' official terms classify the Starbucks name, logo, and related graphics as trademarks or registered trademarks and expressly prohibit their use without prior written permission. That supports a non-public-domain clearance conclusion; trademark protection is not treated as expiring through the ordinary copyright term.

citations.title: about.starbucks.com
excerpts: Our Founders We've come a long way since our original store opened in 1971, but our founders' vision is still alive and well. Friends since their University of San Francisco days, Gerald Baldwin, a former English teacher, Gordon Bowker, a writer, and Zev Siegl, a history teacher, were three 20-somethings who were passionate about the arts, fine food, good wine and, of course, great coffee. They started Starbucks because they wanted Seattle to have access to the delicious dark-roasted coffee that they loved—but had to go out of town to find. Investing $1,350 apiece and borrowing $5,000 from a bank, they took a name from classic literature and opened our first store in April 1971.

citations.title: How Starbucks Went Viral From Game Of Thrones Product Placement Snafu
excerpts: How Much That Product Placement Of The Cup Would Have Cost Starbucks In Game Of Thrones** And the hot topic of the week – what made our agency go viral in the media, is the question of how much WOULD have that cup cost to place in a show like _Game of Thrones_ if Starbucks HAD wanted to pay for a placement. And of course, if the show wasn’t set thousands of years ago in practically another world where dragons exist. That comes down to a few factors. For one, the audience size. The bigger the audience reach, the more realistic it is that a brand is going to want to pay higher dollars for a placement. And of course there is the star factor. Brands like being in content that has well known actors or characters to be associated with. And then of course, it also comes down to the brand exposure opportunity. * Is it a storyline? Well that will cost more. Is it a location where the action takes place? That means the production either has to build the set, or haul their people over to that location – which costs real money to do, and a brand is going to have to compensate for that. Is it a prop? If the actor is touching it, driving it or wearing it – that can be a higher premium. Or is it a set dressing item? Or signage? And it can get competitive. Especially with franchise properties or TV series that have lasted more than one season. It's important to understand that most brands don’t like taking chances. And betting on a new film or TV show, that isn’t proven, can be a big leap of faith. Even though the dollars it would cost to participate are typically less than one or two national TV commercials, and always going to get a bigger reach than what those commercial spots would be. So what I’m saying is that brands in a large part are entirely missing out when they won't take chances on unproven properties. If you are looking at blockbuster films – which is what _Game of Thrones_ is comparable to (or the Super Bowl) – from Marvel’s _Black Panther_ , the _Avengers_ to the DC Comics world of _Superman_ , _Wonder Woman_ , _Batman_ and _Aquaman_ , or the _Transformers_ franchise which gets most of their brand dollars from China now, or even Netflix’s _House of Cards_ which in its heyday commanded a very pretty penny to participate – then it’s going to cost somewhere most probably from $250 thousand to $1 million or even more for a 'brand integration'. But it also means taking in to consideration what character is with the product. Is the logo clear and identifiable. How long the brand will be in the scene.

citations.title: How Starbucks Went Viral From Game Of Thrones Product Placement Snafu
excerpts: * * **And How Hollywood Branded Joined The Viral Moment** If you haven't heard, someone accidentally left a coffee cup on the set of Game of Thrones while filming, and it made an appearance in the final edit of the 4th episode - causing quite a stir among people talking and joking about the cup, to the chagrin of HBO. So many people assumed that it was a Starbucks cup (which we now know it wasn't - in fact [Paper Cup in Belfast](https://www.facebook.com/papercuptitanicquarter/) appears to hold that honor) that it became a viral conversation and earned Starbucks BILLIONS of media impressions. And when I was interviewed about the blunder by Market Watch, then Business Insider, CNBC and Money... it turned into quite the viral story for our agency. As of today's blog posting, Hollywood Branded has earned over 3 billion media impressions at a tune of over $50 million media dollar value. Yep, it's a little unreal. **In this blog post, Hollywood Branded shares five of the most asked questions by reporters about Starbuck's perceived product placement appearance in Game of Thrones, and more details on the resulting worldwide PR phenomena.** * * * GOT Starbucks * * * **Wins Are Coming** As soon as the 4th episode of Game of Thrones aired, besides discussing the all important question of who will claim the iron throne... was what cup of coffee they'll be enjoying while sitting on it. The accidental coffee cup placement is a PR bonanza bigger than anything anyone expected. Even our own agency has benefited massively. The first article I was interviewed for by [MarketWatch](https://www.marketwatch.com/story/that-game-of-thrones-coffee-cup-is-worth-at-least-250000-in-product-placement-for-starbucks-2019-05-06) went viral. Then came another interview opportunity with [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/game-of-thrones-coffee-cup-earns-starbucks-millions-in-free-publicity-2019-5?r=US&IR=T&utm_content=buffer8f861&utm_medium=social&utm_source=facebook.com&utm_campaign=buffer-food) , and another with [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2019/05/07/starbucks-got-2point3-billion-in-free-advertising-from-game-of-thrones-gaffe.html) which again went viral – each building upon the former. And the articles and videos keep coming. The comments I have provided, my name and Hollywood Branded, the agency I own, has now been published by over 300 media outlets. And it is still growing. As of Wednesday morning, Hollywood Branded had received over a billion impressions online and TV around the world. That is crazy and pretty unheard of for an agency. The PR value was over $14 million dollars and those numbers are so staggering that it is hard to fully grasp the impact. Think about it – a billion media impressions? All over the world, in literally every country, and that’s not even counting the social media impact. Or the TV impact, as we were not measuring that - or the print mentions from all corners of the world. Critical Mention 3 days later, our agency reached over 3 billion media impressions to a tune of $55 million media value. And it is still growing - and will continue to grow for some time. Because that is the beauty of the internet and pop culture. It's a staggering amount of impressions. Here's a Facebook video [Money Magazine](https://www.facebook.com/MoneyMagazine/videos/444499419639019/) made about my comments on the placement. But then let’s take a look at the metrics for Starbucks. These aren’t made up numbers – they are provided by the PR analytics tool our agency subscribes to – [Critical Mention,](https://www.criticalmention.com/) a very respected third party source. All I have to do is search key words and digital articles, radio and TV mentions are listed with the reach and a description. Here are some quick numbers we pulled that will already be bigger by the time you're reading this: * Right now, the total online value is $3 billion dollar for Starbucks. That is with a reach of 53 billion online news audience around the world – at least in the countries the software monitors language from, which is a lot. And 1 billion TV impressions across the US on a national TV show. We don’t have TV tracking in other countries, but it is over another billion media value in the US alone. And there have been over 17,000 press clips worldwide and growing, globally. Plus all the social media – hundreds of thousands of posts and shares. And word of mouth chatter. We aren’t even measuring either. And the print coverage we aren't tracking.

Starbucks is not typically known for doing a lot of paid placement in scripted content (well... they DID do Will & Grace) – except for reality television series like The Voice which we wrote about in this blog . Anytime you see their cups in TV shows or movies, it is much like what we do for our client [Coffee Beanery](https://www.coffeebeanery.com/) – free, based on relationships, and because we are often providing complimentary coffee beans for the production to have, as that can be an expensive item that adds up quickly, that productions like to get for free when possible. Will_and_Grace_Starbucks And so many TV shows don’t actually allow paid product placement. Of course this is not relevant as 1) it wasn’t Starbucks and 2) Games of Thrones would not be an appropriate canvas for an in show brand deal based on the time period. * * * **5\. How Much That Product Placement Of The Cup Would Have Cost Starbucks In Game Of Thrones** And the hot topic of the week – what made our agency go viral in the media, is the question of how much WOULD have that cup cost to place in a show like _Game of Thrones_ if Starbucks HAD wanted to pay for a placement. And of course, if the show wasn’t set thousands of years ago in practically another world where dragons exist. That comes down to a few factors. For one, the audience size. The bigger the audience reach, the more realistic it is that a brand is going to want to pay higher dollars for a placement. And of course there is the star factor. Brands like being in content that has well known actors or characters to be associated with. And then of course, it also comes down to the brand exposure opportunity. * Is it a storyline? Well that will cost more. Is it a location where the action takes place? That means the production either has to build the set, or haul their people over to that location – which costs real money to do, and a brand is going to have to compensate for that. Is it a prop? If the actor is touching it, driving it or wearing it – that can be a higher premium. Or is it a set dressing item? Or signage? And it can get competitive. Especially with franchise properties or TV series that have lasted more than one season. It's important to understand that most brands don’t like taking chances. And betting on a new film or TV show, that isn’t proven, can be a big leap of faith. Even though the dollars it would cost to participate are typically less than one or two national TV commercials, and always going to get a bigger reach than what those commercial spots would be. So what I’m saying is that brands in a large part are entirely missing out when they won't take chances on unproven properties. If you are looking at blockbuster films – which is what _Game of Thrones_ is comparable to (or the Super Bowl) – from Marvel’s _Black Panther_ , the _Avengers_ to the DC Comics world of _Superman_ , _Wonder Woman_ , _Batman_ and _Aquaman_ , or the _Transformers_ franchise which gets most of their brand dollars from China now, or even Netflix’s _House of Cards_ which in its heyday commanded a very pretty penny to participate – then it’s going to cost somewhere most probably from $250 thousand to $1 million or even more for a 'brand integration'. But it also means taking in to consideration what character is with the product. Is the logo clear and identifiable. How long the brand will be in the scene.

DHC's published terms prohibit uses likely to cause confusion or disparage/discredit DHC and state that no trademark license is granted for the website materials, but they do not provide a film/television approval process.

item.title: DMM Bitcoin
item.description: The DMM Bitcoin logo is visible on a digital billboard featuring a woman's face.
item.evidence: The logo is visible on the billboard below the DHC sign.

holders.name: 株式会社DMM Bitcoin (DMM Bitcoin Co., Ltd.)
holders.contact: DMM Group corporate/media inquiry form
holders.notes: The company is the last publicly identified operator associated with the DMM Bitcoin service and is named in the official transfer notice. The service ended on 8 March 2025. Current registered ownership of the word mark or logo, and any assignment after closure, is not confirmed. Clear the exact logo artwork and the DMM Bitcoin name separately if applicable.

holders.name: 合同会社DMM.com (DMM.com LLC)
holders.territory: Worldwide, if authorized; exact trademark territory not confirmed
holders.contact: DMM Group corporate/media inquiry form for corporate and media customers
holders.notes: DMM.com LLC is the DMM Group entity publicly described as overseeing the DMM service business. The available evidence does not expressly establish that it owns the DMM Bitcoin trademark, but it is the best-supported public routing point for a brand-use approval request.

holders.name: SBI VCトレード株式会社 (SBI VC Trade Co., Ltd.)
holders.contact: SBI VC Trade customer/contact channels
holders.notes: SBI VC Trade received DMM Bitcoin customer accounts, Japanese-yen and spot-crypto assets, and related transaction records. The retrieved agreement does not show that SBI VC Trade acquired the DMM Bitcoin trademark, logo, or entertainment-approval rights; do not treat it as the trademark licensor without separate written confirmation.

finding.public_domain_rationale: The evidence does not establish that the particular DMM Bitcoin logo is an uncopyrighted or public-domain work in the United States. The end of the DMM Bitcoin service and the transfer of customer assets do not place the brand or logo in the public domain. Because the visible material is a branded trademark/logo and its artwork authorship, publication, and copyright history are unresolved, its copyright status should be treated as unclear while trademark permission remains required.
finding.territory_notes: The requested licence is worldwide, all media, in perpetuity. No public territorial split or worldwide trademark grant was identified. The 2025 transfer to SBI VC Trade is documented as a transfer of DMM Bitcoin customer accounts, assets, and related records—not as a transfer of the DMM Bitcoin trademark or logo. Obtain worldwide written approval from the current trademark proprietor or its authorized DMM Group representative.
finding.licensing_precedent: No publicly documented prior film or television licence, product-placement agreement, or reported fee for the DMM Bitcoin name or logo was identified. The available official material concerns service termination, customer-asset transfer, and general DMM corporate/media contact rather than entertainment licensing.
unresolved: The current registered proprietor of the exact DMM Bitcoin word mark and billboard logo has not been confirmed from a current trademark-register record.
The chain of title from DMM Bitcoin Co., Ltd. to any DMM Group entity, if different, is not publicly documented in the retrieved material.
The 2025 SBI VC Trade agreement is documented for customer accounts, assets, and transaction records, but its treatment of DMM Bitcoin trademark and logo rights is not stated.
It has not been established whether DMM Bitcoin Co., Ltd. remains active, is in liquidation, or has assigned its intellectual-property rights.

No DMM Bitcoin-specific film/television approval department, licensing representative, or entertainment-use policy was identified; the available DMM contact route is a general corporate/media inquiry form.
The exact first-publication date, author, and copyright status of the particular DMM Bitcoin logo artwork shown on the billboard are unknown.

basis.reasoning: The official DMM Bitcoin notice confirms that the service ended and customer assets were transferred, but it does not state that the name or logo entered the public domain or that the billboard artwork is uncopyrighted. Accordingly, copyright public-domain status is unresolved rather than affirmatively established.

excerpts: いつも当社サービスをご利用いただきありがとうございます。 SBIホールディングス株式会社（本社：東京都港区、代表取締役会長兼社長：北尾 吉孝）の連結子会社で暗号資産交換業を営む当社は、2024年12月2日に公表した [「DMM Bitcoinからの口座・預かり資産移管に向けた基本合意に関するお知らせ」](https://www.sbivc.co.jp/newsview/1zkj8mf5x3y) の通り、株式会社DMM Bitcoin（本社：東京都中央区、代表取締役：松田 昇樹、以下DMM Bitcoin）のお客さまの口座及び預かり資産の移管を受け入れることについて、本契約を締結したことをお知らせいたします。 本契約により、DMM Bitcoinのお客さまの口座および預かり資産は、2025年3月8日（土）に当社に移管される予定となります。移管に際して、お客さまが事前に当社の口座開設を行っていただく必要はなく、当社側にて口座開設を実施予定となります。 移管前後におけるDMM Bitcoinと当社とのサービス差異、及び条件等につきましては、以下の通りとなります。 **■サービス差異** ＜現物取引＞ 現物取引については、現在当社の取扱いがなくDMM Bitcoinにて取扱っている14銘柄を、当社にて移管日までに取扱い開始する予定です※。暗号資産同士の交換（ETH/BTC）は、現時点では取扱い予定はありません。 ※やむを得ない事情により、移管日までに取扱いができない場合があります。 ＜レバレッジ取引＞ レバレッジ取引については、現在当社の取扱いがなくDMM Bitcoinにて取扱っているペアは、現時点では取扱い予定はありません。また、レバレッジ取引の未決済ポジションは移管の対象外です。 なお、当社はDMM Bitcoinと同様に、保有している暗号資産をレバレッジ取引の証拠金として活用できる数少ない暗号資産交換業者・第一種金融商品取引業者となり、レバレッジ手数料ではなくファンディングレートを採用していることから、お客さまがポジションによって日次で手数料を受け取ることも可能となります。 ※当社のレバレッジ取引のサービス内容は [こちら](https://www.sbivc.co.jp/services/leverage) をご確認ください。 ＜ステーキング＞ 当社のステーキング対象銘柄については、特段のお手続き不要で、移管後、自動的にステーキングの対象となります。DMM BitcoinにてETH、AVAX、OAS、FLR、HBARを保有されているお客さまは、2025年3月8日より当社にてステーキング対象となりますので、継続保有されることで2025年4月上旬に初回のステーキング報酬が付与される予定となります。 ※当社のステーキングのサービス内容は [こちら](https://www.sbivc.co.jp/services/staking) をご確認ください。 **■移管対象者** 2025年3月4日（火）時点でDMM Bitcoinに口座開設済の全てのお客さまが対象となります。なお、本移管について、当社における新規口座開設のお手続きをお客さまに実施いただく必要はありません。 ※お客さまの口座登録情報、本人確認書類及びマイナンバー情報についても、法令に基づき適切に移管します。 **■移管対象の預かり資産** ・日本円 ・現物暗号資産 ※DMM Bitcoinで実施された取引に関する取引報告書等についても、移管に伴い当社が継承します。 **■DMM Bitcoinからの口座・預かり資産移管について特設サイト** [https://www.sbivc.co.jp/dmm_vct](https://www.sbivc.co.jp/dmm_vct) 当社ではSBI グループが掲げる「顧客中心主義」に基づき、お客さま視点に立ったサービスを実現してまいります。今後ともご愛顧賜りますよう、お願い申し上げます。

excerpts: DMM Bitcoin サービス終了のお知らせ DMM Bitcoinのサービスは、2025年3月8日をもちまして終了いたしました。当社お客様の口座及び預かり資産は、SBI VCトレード株式会社へ移管しております。今後のお問い合せ等につきましては、 [SBI VCトレード株式会社](https://www.sbivc.co.jp/) へお願いいたします。長い間、ご利用ありがとうございました。 Q&A Q.アプリを開こうとすると404エラーが表示されます。 A.DMM Bitcoinのサービスは、2025年3月8日(土)をもちまして終了いたしましたので、ご利用いただくことができません。お客様の口座及び預かり資産(日本円、暗号資産)は、2025年3月8日(土)に全てSBI VCトレード株式会社へ移管しております。今後は、SBI VCトレード株式会社のアプリをご利用ください。 Q.初回ログイン設定の案内が届いていません。移管パスワードがわかりません。 A.移管パスワードが記載された、初回ログイン設定に関するご案内につきましては、2025年3月3日(月)にSBI VCトレード株式会社より、当社ご登録のメインメールアドレス宛にお送りしております。当社ご登録のメインメールアドレスが変更になっている等でご案内がお手元に届いていないお客様は、メールアドレス変更及び再送付につきまして、SBI VCトレード株式会社へお問い合わせください。 Q.移管手続きはどうすればよいですか。私の資産はどうなりましたか。 A.お客様の口座及び預かり資産(日本円、暗号資産)は、2025年3月8日(土)に全てSBI VCトレード株式会社へ移管が完了しております。お客様の資産をご確認いただくためには、SBI VCトレード株式会社にて初回ログイン設定のお手続きが必要となります。2025年3月3日(月)にSBI VCトレード株式会社より、移管パスワードが記載された、初回ログイン設定に関するご案内を、当社ご登録のメインメールアドレス宛にお送りしておりますので、メールに記載された手順に沿って、初回ログイン設定をお願いします。

excerpts: DMM Bitcoin サービス終了のお知らせ DMM Bitcoinのサービスは、2025年3月8日をもちまして終了いたしました。当社お客様の口座及び預かり資産は、SBI VCトレード株式会社へ移管しております。今後のお問い合せ等につきましては、 [SBI VCトレード株式会社](https://www.sbivc.co.jp/) へお願いいたします。長い間、ご利用ありがとうございました。 Q&A Q.アプリを開こうとすると404エラーが表示されます。 A.DMM Bitcoinのサービスは、2025年3月8日(土)をもちまして終了いたしましたので、ご利用いただくことができません。お客様の口座及び預かり資産(日本円、暗号資産)は、2025年3月8日(土)に全てSBI VCトレード株式会社へ移管しております。今後は、SBI VCトレード株式会社のアプリをご利用ください。 Q.初回ログイン設定の案内が届いていません。移管パスワードがわかりません。 A.移管パスワードが記載された、初回ログイン設定に関するご案内につきましては、2025年3月3日(月)にSBI VCトレード株式会社より、当社ご登録のメインメールアドレス宛にお送りしております。当社ご登録のメインメールアドレスが変更になっている等でご案内がお手元に届いていないお客様は、メールアドレス変更及び再送付につきまして、SBI VCトレード株式会社へお問い合わせください。 Q.移管手続きはどうすればよいですか。私の資産はどうなりましたか。 A.お客様の口座及び預かり資産(日本円、暗号資産)は、2025年3月8日(土)に全てSBI VCトレード株式会社へ移管が完了しております。お客様の資産をご確認いただくためには、SBI VCトレード株式会社にて初回ログイン設定のお手続きが必要となります。2025年3月3日(月)にSBI VCトレード株式会社より、移管パスワードが記載された、初回ログイン設定に関するご案内を、当社ご登録のメインメールアドレス宛にお送りしておりますので、メールに記載された手順に沿って、初回ログイン設定をお願いします。

News Hit and LIVE BOARD collaborate for the first time with 16 outdoor screens!Digital OOH ads based on impressions (VAC) on Hit Visions and Metropolitan Expressway Digital LED Board are now available. 18 Nov 24 Press Release LIVE BOARD, INC., will connect and link "Shibuhachi Hit Vision," "Tsutaya Ebisubashi Hit Vision," and "Metropolitan Expressway Digital LED Board" managed and operated by Hit Co., Ltd., which specializes in outdoor advertising, to the LIVE BOARD Marketplace\* from October 28, 2024 (Monday). **◆Hit, which specializes in outdoor advertising, and LIVE BOARD collaborate for the first time on 16 outdoor screens.** Hit, established in February 1991, is a leading company in outdoor advertising. Hit has many digital signage systems installed along major roads such as the Metropolitan Expressway and Shin-Midosuji Avenue, as well as the largest digital signage systems in downtown areas in the Kanto and Kansai regions. Among them are the high-impact "Shibuhachi Hit Vision," "Tsutaya Ebisubashi Hit Vision," and "Metropolitan Expressway Digital LED Board," which are linked to LIVE BOARD to make it easier for advertisers to place their ads in the OOH industry. LIVE BOARD aims to support further expansion of the OOH market, adding additional value through strategic initiatives that promote the realization of ad delivery adapted to diverse audiences. \* This refers to the entire DOOH advertising space (inventory) handled by LIVE BOARD, including its own and other companies'. **◆Media Details** **\- Shibuhachi Hit Vision** 241118_1.jpg Located in the Hachiko Square in Shibuya, Tokyo, this is one of the largest single-panel digital signage for advertising in Japan. Date of connection: October 28, 2024 Location: 2-3-2 Dogenzaka, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo Size: H17400 × W24400(㎜) Number of screens: 1 Display hours: 7:00 - 24:00 Audio: Available For Mmore Ddetails,: [check here](https://www.hit-ad.co.jp/english/) \*The following material is for reference only and owned by the media vendor, the prices and information may differ from what Live Board is offering. **\- Tsutaya Ebisubashi Hit Vision** 241118_2.jpg Located in Dotonbori, the heart of Osaka, this is one of the largest digital signage for advertising in Japan. With displays using both the upper and lower screens, it expands the creative possibilities.

holders.notes: G.U. CO., LTD. designs, manufactures, and retails GU-branded goods. It is the most relevant operating-company contact for a GU-specific request, but public materials do not expressly state that it alone grants worldwide film and television approvals.

holders.name: GU USA LLC
holders.contact: GU USA customer-service contact form; guusa_contactus@gu-global.com is published for customer-service inquiries
holders.notes: The GU US terms identify GU USA LLC as the contracting entity and state that express written consent from GU is required for commercial use of GU site content, logos, and proprietary information. This is a US contact route, not a confirmed worldwide entertainment-licensing office.

finding.public_domain_rationale: GU is a commercial trademark and brand, not a conventional copyrighted work for which a public-domain determination ordinarily applies. The available materials identify GU as a brand of Fast Retailing and state that GU logos and related marks are protected trademarks. Because the specific logo's creation/publication date and any applicable copyright status were not established, the correct clearance answer is unclear rather than public domain.
finding.territory_notes: The intended use is worldwide, all media, in perpetuity. No public territory-specific licensing split or blanket worldwide entertainment licence was identified. The GU US terms require express written consent for commercial use of GU logos and proprietary information; for a worldwide release, approval should be obtained from the relevant GU/Fast Retailing rights function, not assumed from US customer-service terms alone.
finding.licensing_precedent: No publicly documented GU licence or product-placement agreement for film or television, and no reported GU-specific fee, was identified.
unresolved: The exact trademark registration and ownership position for the specific GU logo appearing on the brown shopping bag in each intended territory has not been conclusively established from the available public records.
No dedicated film/television brand-approval department or global entertainment-licensing contact was publicly identified.
No public fee schedule or documented GU film/television licence precedent was identified.
The relationship between Fast Retailing Co., Ltd., G.U. CO., LTD., and GU USA LLC for approving worldwide audiovisual depictions is not expressly allocated in the public materials.

basis.reasoning: The GU terms state that GU logos and marks are protected trademarks and that infringement is not permitted, while the trademark notice attributes other site trademarks to Fast Retailing or legitimate right holders. These sources do not establish that the depicted logo is public domain; they support an unclear/non-public-domain clearance status.
